items.summary: The Board of Supervisors convened for its regular meeting on January 14, 2025. The clerk took roll call, confirming all members were present, followed by an Ohlone land acknowledgment and the Pledge of Allegiance.
The clerk read general communications, including information on meeting broadcasts, ADA accessibility requests, language assistance, and procedures for public comment.
The Board considered the approval of meeting minutes from November 19, December 3, and December 10, 2024. The minutes were approved unanimously on a roll call vote.

Supervisor Dorsey presented an ordinance amending the Planning Code and Zoning Map for the 30 Van Ness Avenue Special Use District to improve project feasibility and jumpstart construction on a stalled multi-family housing development. Following committee discussion and non-substantive amendments confirmed by the City Attorney, the Board approved the amendments and passed the ordinance on first reading.

items.summary: Members of the public addressed the Board during general public comment. Prominent topics included outrage and concern regarding the impending closure of the Fillmore Safeway grocery store and its impact on the community, support for special police training and reentry programs, neighborhood safety, and city accountability.

items.summary: The Board considered an approval of a 90-day extension for Planning Commission review of window replacement standards. The extension was adopted unanimously without committee reference.
The Board approved the motion to hold a Committee of the Whole to consider urgent accept and expend resolutions for federal grants, along with the consent agenda items.

The Board convened as a Committee of the Whole to conduct a special hearing considering 15 urgent accept and expend resolutions across six city departments to secure over $133 million in federal grant funds.
The Board of Supervisors sat as a Committee of the Whole to hear department presentations on urgent accept and expend grant resolutions prior to returning to the regular board meeting.
The Committee of the Whole hearing was concluded and reported back to the full Board of Supervisors.
The Board considered a resolution to accept and expend a $2,700,000 FEMA grant through Cal OES for the Pier 94/96 Seismic Improvements Project. The resolution was amended and adopted unanimously.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the acceptance and expenditure of a $159,900 grant from FEMA through Cal OES to establish an Engineering with Nature working group. The item was amended and adopted without objection.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the Department of the Environment to accept and expend a $19,994,217 federal grant from the Department of Energy for building performance standards. Following discussion on staffing and position authority, the resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Department of the Environment to accept and expend $284,800 from the US Department of Energy to fund a community engagement liaison position. The resolution was amended regarding position funding conditions and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Department of Public Health to accept and expend $791,433 in vocational rehabilitation services grant funds from the US Department of Education. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution accepting and expending a $14,996,876 US Department of Transportation grant to boost electric vehicle charging in San Francisco. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively approving the acceptance and expenditure of $223,673 in CalAIM JI PATH funding from the California Department of Health Care Services for individuals transitioning out of incarceration. The resolution was amended and adopted.

Supervisor Chan moved to refer the Visitacion Avenue Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety Improvement Project grant resolution of $750,000 back to the Budget and Finance Committee because it is a state grant not subject to federal urgency. The motion to refer passed without objection.

The Board considered a resolution authorizing the acceptance and expenditure of a $20,000,000 grant from the US Department of Transportation for the Bayview Connections Harney Way BRT and cycletrack project. The resolution was amended and adopted.
The Board considered a resolution retroactively approving an $832,804 grant from the California Department of Social Services for Refugee Support Services. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the Recreation and Park Department to accept and expend $1,493,692 from the California Department of Parks and Recreation for the Twin Peaks Promenade Project. The resolution was amended to place funds on reserve and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the Department of Public Health to accept and expend $13,635,302 from the CDC for STD prevention and control. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the Department of Public Health to accept and expend a grant increase to $104,508 from the NIH through UT Southwestern Medical Center for clinical trials network research. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the acceptance and expenditure of a $1,600,000 grant from the Department of Justice for the Comprehensive Opioid, Stimulant, and Substance Use Site-Based Program. The resolution was amended and adopted.

The Board considered a resolution to apply for, accept, and expend a $55,386,000 grant from the EPA Clean Ports Program to fund the San Francisco waterfront emissions-free ferry system. The resolution was amended to place funds on reserve and adopted.
The meeting was adjourned in memory of Colonel Peter.
